title: Relative-Entropy Flow Across the Page Transition
abstract: We develop a computational framework for the quantum relative entropy based on the replica trick and apply it to analyze the evaporation process method of Jackiw-Teitelboim black holes. We show that the relative entropies between the exact radiation state and the Hawking saddle state and the replica wormholes saddle state quantify information-theoretic costs inherent to coarse-grained semiclassical descriptions. During evaporation, the relative entropy for the Hawking saddle increases monotonically, reflecting a progressively higher thermodynamic cost of sustaining the Hawking description. Conversely, the relative entropy associated with the replica wormholes saddle decreases, which indicates that the description of connected geometries becomes progressively more accurate. Moreover, the sign of the difference between the two quantities reverses precisely at the Page time, providing an information-theoretic diagnosis for the transition between competing gravitational saddles. Our results recast the Page transition as a flow of relative entropy costs between competing semi-classical descriptions, revealing an information-theoretic structure underlying the emergence of effective irreversibility in coarse-grained black hole evaporation.
summary: This work reinterprets the black hole Page transition using quantum relative entropy, treating it as a flow of information-theoretic costs between two competing semi-classical gravitational descriptions. By analyzing how the relative entropy changes over time, the authors establish an information-theoretic criterion that precisely diagnoses the transition point where the description shifts from the Hawking saddle to the replica wormholes saddle.
main_problem: The paper analyzes the information-theoretic structure underlying the Page transition during black hole evaporation by comparing competing semi-classical gravitational descriptions.
main_result: The Page transition is recast as a flow of relative entropy costs between the Hawking saddle and the replica wormholes saddle, with the sign change of the difference in relative entropy diagnosing the transition.
method: The authors develop a computational framework using the quantum relative entropy, calculated via the replica trick, to quantify the information-theoretic cost associated with approximating the exact quantum state.
model_or_system: The analysis is performed on Jackiw-Teitelboim (JT) gravity applied to an End-of-the-World (EoW) brane (PSSY model), modeling black hole evaporation.
key_observables: Relative Entropy (RE) between the exact radiation state and the two saddle states, and the difference in these relative entropies ($\Delta S$).
important_parameters: The Page time, which marks the sign reversal of $\Delta S$; the replica index $n$ and the large $k$ limit.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the support of the exact state is contained within the support of the saddle states, and the effective irreversibility is not taken to imply a breakdown of fundamental unitarity.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the time evolution of the relative entropies for both the Hawking and wormhole saddles, showing the monotonic increase of the Hawking cost and the decay of the wormhole cost, culminating in a sign change for $\Delta S$ at the Page time.
paper_structure: The paper builds the framework by defining the RE using the replica trick, applies it to the two competing semiclassical saddles ($\sigma_{	ext{Haw}}$ and $\sigma_{	ext{WH}}$), derives explicit time-dependent expressions for the REs, and finally interprets the flow of these costs across the Page transition.
why_interesting: While focused on gravity, the use of relative entropy flow to diagnose a transition point based on the relative efficiency of two competing descriptions is a powerful, generalizable tool for analyzing non-equilibrium processes in complex quantum systems.
